title: The productivity cost of sovereign default: evidence from the European debt crisis
abstract: The authors estimate the productivity cost of sovereign default using a continuous-time model in which a government’s default decision can shift the regime governing total factor productivity. They calibrate the model with financial-market information for European countries during 2009–2012 and compare productivity dynamics under default and non-default regimes. The estimated decline in productivity ranges from 3.70 to 5.88 percent, depending on the calibration. The model also reproduces observed declines in GDP growth and subsequent recoveries, and helps explain why fiscal multipliers may be small during sovereign debt crises.
